thread:
incident-bot: PAGED: High 5xx rate observed in eu-west-1 for Hosted API and Dedicated pools. Severity: P1. Pager duty: Emma (oncall-sre), Rajesh (oncall-platform).

emma (oncall-sre): I'm seeing a sudden spike in 5xx from the edge -> origin path, starting ~3375002400. Affected: hosted API endpoints in eu-west-1 and several Dedicated pools pinned to the region.

kai (infra): Confirmed from ELB metrics: target group healthy_count OK but 5xx_count up ~20x. Looking at network errors between ELB and control-plane proxies.

rajesh (oncall-platform): Any signs of STS/KMS errors? Our auth layer talks to STS for temporary creds when Dedicated pools spin up.

emma (oncall-sre): Good call — auth errors correlate. Sample logs:
```
2026-03-14T09:07:12Z service=auth caller=sts request_id=abc123 status=503 body="ServiceUnavailable"
2026-03-14T09:07:13Z service=edge caller=proxy request_id=def456 status=502 backend=10.1.2.3:504 error="upstream reset"
2026-03-14T09:07:15Z service=dedicated-proxy request_id=ghi789 status=503 error="unable to get creds: STS Throttling"
```

olivia (service-owner): Customers: several mid-market customers reported increased latency and timeouts for chat completions. Any active rollback or routing we can do?

rajesh (oncall-platform): Initiating regional failover to eu-central-1 for non-data-residency customers. Will update routing policy to prefer eu-central and fall back to eu-west if healthy. Command I'll run: `redwoodctl routing update --region-preference eu-central-1 --reason "eu-west-1 elevated 5xx"`

kai (infra): Before full switch, can we selectively drain traffic from Dedicated pools in eu-west-1? I can trigger pool scale-in and mark nodes for fallback. Running: `infractl pool set-drain --pool eu-west-1-dedicated --drain=true`

emma (oncall-sre): I'll throttle incoming new requests at the edge for sensitive customers and enable caching for prompt prefixes to reduce STS calls. Patch: set prefix-KV cache TTL=30s for /v1/generate routes.

incident-bot: New incident ticket created: INC-2026-0823 (link: https://redwood-incidents.internal/inc/INC-2026-0823). Pager duty escalation on-call: Rajesh next.

rajesh (oncall-platform): Update: routing change applied, 27% of traffic shifted to eu-central-1 (canary). Monitoring latency and 5xx now.

emma (oncall-sre): Observability note: we see 5xx rate in eu-west-1 drop ~40% but overall user latency still elevated due to in-flight requests and retries. Adding temporary response headers to identify region: `X-Redwood-Region: eu-central-1` for canaryed traffic.

olivia (service-owner): Notifying impacted customers via status page and support channel. Draft: "We are seeing elevated errors in eu-west-1 caused by AWS regional auth/ELB anomalies. Mitigation: traffic is being routed to eu-central-1 for most workloads; Dedicated pools are being drained and shifted where possible."

kai (infra): I opened an AWS support case (SR# 1234567890) with ELB/STS team and linked logs. AWS status shows a degraded impact to a subset of eu-west-1 auth endpoints: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incident/ELB/2026-03-14

emma (oncall-sre): Quick test command for ops: `curl -v https://eu-west-1.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'` — response shows 503 in eu-west-1 canary but eu-central returns 200. Example:
```
* Connected to eu-west-1.api.redwood.ai (52.16.xx.xx) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
< Content-Type: application/json
< {"error":"upstream_unavailable","code":503}
```

rajesh (oncall-platform): Handing off primary pager to me for the next 2 hours while Emma rotates off. @emma please leave any open runbook notes in the incident ticket.

emma (oncall-sre): Copy. Leaving notes: attempted prefix caching, route canary, drained two dedicated node pools, created AWS SR, notified affected customers.

pagerduty-bot: Acknowledged: handoff to Rajesh at 09:25 UTC.

rajesh (oncall-platform): Next steps: 1) Continue canary to 50% traffic to eu-central. 2) Increase retries for short-lived auth calls with exponential backoff to avoid thundering herd. 3) For Dedicated pools that must remain in eu-west due to compliance, add local retry and extend keepalive. 4) Coordinate with SRE on scaling edge and queue depth.

kai (infra): Ran `infractl conn-dump --region eu-west-1` — lots of connections in CLOSE_WAIT to proxy instances, possible downstream overload. I'll recycle 4 proxies with zero-downtime restart.

olivia (service-owner): Customer impact estimate: ~15% of Hosted API requests in eu-west-1 observed 5xx during peak interval; 4 Dedicated customers experienced degraded throughput (their pools were pinned). I'll prepare a post-incident update for the status page once we have root cause confirmation from AWS.

rajesh (oncall-platform): Can everyone drop quick updates here as changes are made so I can stitch timeline? I'll keep this thread as the source-of-truth.

emma (oncall-sre): change: cache TTL applied, two proxies recycled, edge canary bumped to 50%. Observed 5xx rate reduced another ~30% in eu-west-1 but still above baseline.

kai (infra): Completed proxy restarts. No crash loops, latency of health checks stable.

incident-bot: NOTE: Auto-silenced non-critical alerts for the affected region to reduce noise.

rajesh (oncall-platform): AWS responded on SR: ELB partial control-plane degradation affecting target management and STS token issuance. They are working on remediation; estimate 1-2 hours. They recommended continuing routing to healthy regions.

olivia (service-owner): Good. Let's prepare an RCA checklist: - timeline & impact, - mitigation steps, - permanent mitigations (more aggressive cross-region fallback, reduce STS sync points), - action items for Dedicated pool SLA customers.

emma (oncall-sre): Action item created: RJ-2345 "Improve regional failover for auth-dependent flows" assigned to platform team.

rajesh (oncall-platform): Final update for now: production traffic is stable at 60% eu-central / 40% eu-west after canary; 5xx trending down. AWS says they have a fix in flight. I'll continue to monitor and escalate if it regresses. If we see any Dedicated pool owners still impacted, escalate to Account Execs and consider crediting affected customers.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-0823 status updated: Monitoring -> Mitigated (partial). Next: postmortem in 72h.

olivia (service-owner): Thanks team. Please add any remaining notes to the incident ticket. We'll keep the postmortem focused on dependency risk and stronger SLAs for auth/ELB.

emma (oncall-sre): leaving thread — thanks.

rajesh (oncall-platform): staying on monitoring for the next hour. If no regression, I'll close the incident and draft an incident summary.

incident-bot: Thread closed for active paging. If errors reappear, this thread will reopen.
